content.comment_body: Hi everyone, I can access the [product_name] web server using standard browsers. However, when I try Safari on iPhone or iPad (iOS7), the page remains blank. Any advice would be appreciated. My [product_name] is online at [url] for testing – please use it responsibly!

Hello, I can view it on my PC using Firefox and also on my Samsung smartphone via Chrome. I'll see if I can find someone with an iPhone to test. Note: I can't log in without the password. Hope that's helpful.

I did secure it with a password. I've tested with MS Explorer, Samsung Galaxy 5, Blackberry Q10 and all worked fine. Still, iPhone and iPad on iOS7 only display a blank page. Would appreciate it if anyone can try with iPhone or iPad running iOS7 or iOS8.

Hi, I had two colleagues with iPhones – one on iOS7 and one on iOS8. Both managed to reach your login page, though it didn't load properly the first time. For iOS7, we needed to clear old cached images. For iOS8, visiting Google first (to check internet) made it work. Here’s a picture from the iOS7 device. So the setup does work. Check your internet first, then try your [product_name] page; clear old cookies and browsing history as well. Good luck!
Thanks so much! I'll follow the same steps.

Hello again, If anyone else wants to access my [product_name] page with iPhone on iOS7, you're welcome. I tried the steps again, but both devices still only showed a blank page. The page will be available for the next few days for testing. Thanks.

The issue is resolved. You need to enable cookies, clear cached images, clear browsing history, check internet connectivity, and avoid using private browsing (translated as 'navigazione privata' in Italian). Big thanks to [user_name].
I can view the main page, but clicking 'log on' gives a 'web server is disabled' message. How can I enable it?
Only the main page is accessible; I set up a login password for security.

You can enable the web server and relevant features through the Comfortsoft Tools menu. This worked for me, though advanced options like program access and parameter changes weren't available as I expected.

Hi [user_name], Here's what you can do with the web server: 1. Operator actions similar to what’s possible on [product_name] or with a compatible operator panel. 2. Carry out programmed operations via cursor keys or function keys if configured. 3. Modify parameter settings if they're displayed and editable. More advanced features (like switching modes or program clearing) are restricted for safety since operators may unintentionally change setups. It makes sense to limit access. Also, if you can connect via smartphone, you can use [product_name] configuration software. Remember to activate remote access in the access control settings or it won't work remotely. Hope this helps, [user_name]

Hi everyone, I’m trying to access my [product_name] web server externally as described previously, but haven’t succeeded yet. Access inside my LAN works, but not from outside. Can anyone share the router settings required? I can view your web server without issue, but I’m stuck after trying port forwarding, disabling Firewall and IPSec. Not sure what else to check. Best regards
Solved: Opening port 80 on my router allowed it to work. If this helps anyone, my local IP matches my [product_name]. Best regards
A new question published by [user_name] is now in a separate thread: '[product_name] Web Server, can’t modify any value'. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered compatibility troubles when accessing the [product_name] web server with Safari on iPhone and iPad running iOS7 and iOS8, receiving blank pages. Browsers and devices like PCs and Android phones worked fine. The solution involved enabling cookies, clearing image and browsing caches, checking connectivity, and avoiding private browsing in Safari. The web server could be activated using [product_name] configuration tools, but advanced functions were not available as some users hoped.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth and consistent access to the [product_name] web server on iOS Safari, similar to other platforms, with secure login and comprehensive features available for use.
